scope: Independent CPU-only reanalysis of archived fixed-duration drained diagnostics; no production/harness/queue mutation or service rerun. Raw request counts and timestamps are measured, causal attributions explicitly limited.
current_user_rule: Latest question.md prefers same-condition relative behavior; do not veto solely on local absolute gate failure or one newbad. Correctness/census and chain costs remain explicit.

config_identity.note: A1 and A2 are nonadjacent arms separated by three other arms; equal config is not equal wall-clock arrival or cache history. Raw namespaces differ as required after true flush.

a1_a2_pair.output_content_scope: Raw archive records output counts only, not generated output_ids/text; equal counts does not prove equal generated content.

timestamp_decomposition_note: API dispatch→forward is a scheduler/admission waiting proxy, not measured kernel time. req_time_stats.py:759 freezes forward_entry on the first selected batch (not later chunk continuation); forward→first therefore includes all chunk prefill, prep, launch and intervening scheduling until first token and cannot be called pure GPU latency. Cross client/server components assume a shared clock; observed small negative first-delivery offsets show calibration is imperfect. No clock drift measurement is archived.

closed_loop_gap.proof: Original drive waits frozen gap AFTER previous response completes and renders next prompt, then dispatches. N worker slots dequeue the next chain only after prior chain drive ends. Thus same workload hashes do not fix arrivals: service stalls directly shift later requests, which change competing requests/cache reuse and admit-before-cutoff set. This mechanism is proved by source and residual timestamps; seed of initial tiny service differences remains unidentified.

chain_self_repeat.newbad_admission_component: All5 steady newbad TTFTs are dominated by API→first selected batch waits: A1→A2 waits1.104→137.639s;3.573→96.276s;.734→41.204s;.013→30.795s;6.020→37.522s. Two have exactly equal cache counts and the remaining three change cache counts; exact KDA/host effects not identifiable. Total TTFT and per-request details retained above.

observable_engineering_findings.finding: Opening post-first-token starvation is real and disproportionately harms unweighted mean TPOT for short outputs. First-five short requests have >tens-of-seconds postfirst spans across repeats; inspect opening table.
observable_engineering_findings.contract: Client TPOT includes stalls and token transport after first event; it is not a decoder-only kernel cost.
observable_engineering_findings.candidate: 125 relief0 overrides normal2 and min risk1 to zero decode deferrals, allowing consecutive admitted prefill batches. relief1 supplies a decode opportunity after each extend; an opportunity is not a guaranteed productive decode. This is an authorized parameter test proposal, not measured causality/benefit.
observable_engineering_findings.limits: No same-run batch chronology/relief state log in local archive yet; cannot label all opening stalls as confirmed relief-caused.

observable_engineering_findings.finding: 125 is history-dependent: rate EWMA charges intervals between prefills including decode and retains its rate across true flush; slow RID count is cumulative and latches at80 with gate.10 until flush. Small arrival changes can change relief switching time and cumulative slow count.
observable_engineering_findings.candidate: Observe rate/backlog/slow/relieved/effective interval at each state transition. Do not change reset policy without qualification; retained warmup rate is intentional source contract.
observable_engineering_findings.limits: Actual A1/A2 trip/on/off transitions not observed; same rep16 warmup and successful flush rule out simply carrying raw cache content.

observable_engineering_findings.finding: 236 same IDs show different cached token counts, including large changes; server does genuinely compute different amounts of effective prefix work, despite same expected workload.
observable_engineering_findings.candidate: Correlate cache prefix length, KDA checkpoint availability/host load and eviction reasons with admission batches, instead of optimizing only already-cached pure-decode kernels.
observable_engineering_findings.limits: cached_tokens does not distinguish KV hit from KDA checkpoint hit or host cache; cannot prove KDA miss/eviction or memory pressure from this field alone.

minimum_once_instrument_proposal.scope: One bounded diagnostic stream on an already authorized run, no changes to harness, scoring, input order, gaps, outputs or scheduler decisions; no extra service evaluation requested.
minimum_once_instrument_proposal.server: Use rank0 bounded record per batch: monotonic batch seq/start/end host timestamps, mode, real batch size/new/continued uncached tokens, productive decode count, waiting/running count, cold backlog, rate, slow/seen/tripped/relieved/effective interval, KV/Mamba free slots. Preserve existing ax-125 transitions. Add hashed RID→first-token/decode-batch and cache prefix/KDA checkpoint/hostload reason on misses; sample ring buffer dump on long postfirst stall. Do not synchronize CUDA per step; optional bounded events with later query only if separately approved.
minimum_once_instrument_proposal.transport: Record first and last generated token server monotonic timestamps in diagnostic log, not scored metadata; expose SSE enqueue/send timing only for stalled RID sample. Client raw already gives first/finish and needs no harness change.
minimum_once_instrument_proposal.system: Read-only low-rate1Hz GPU clock/power/temp/utilization and CPU load/steal/RSS/JIT log with shared timestamps; bounded archive budget.
minimum_once_instrument_proposal.why: A single chronology joins arrival→admit→prefill/decode→SSE and identifies lost decode opportunities, checkpoint recomputation, or true system slowdown, rather than inferring them from TPOT alone.

conclusion.proved: Closed-loop completion-driven arrivals and different cache work amplify tiny timing/order differences into distinct service histories. TTFT variability is predominantly admission/scheduling time and chain threshold changes occur in steady phase, not a repeat-wide execution slowdown. TPOT paired median shift is tiny while broad bidirectional tails cancel; do not summarize as generic random noise.
conclusion.unproved: Root cause of initial perturbation, exact share attributable to relief/prefill starvation vs cache/KDA vs hardware/transport cannot be assigned from current raw endpoints alone.
conclusion.07: Relative baseline mean/chain improvement independently confirmed, but added five fixes vs05 have +.033ms matched mean and cannot be claimed a clear further TPOT gain; equal output counts only. P95 and single newbad vsA1 remain costs under latest user rule.
conclusion.protection: Protect true N42 admission/census/output contracts and chain cost; do not seek ranked TPM by forcing more prefills that starve already-decoding short outputs. A1/A2 repeat scale .483ms is much smaller than5.914ms formal gap but cannot be used as formal significance interval.

queue_depth_proxy.limits: Timestamp-derived request interval counts do not expose actual scheduler queue or batch ownership, hostcache waiting, pending continuation, or async runner depth. They should not be called waiting_queue length.
